name: Momentum and LT Reversal
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=4.29 over 1965–2001 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get. Composite: cross-sectional z-score of 6-month momentum minus the z-score of the t-60 to t-13 return, so winners that are long-run losers rank highest. Signal is oriented so the direction the paper predicts scores positive, so a negative observed t means the effect ran backwards on this sample.

name: Momentum in high volume stocks
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=5.78 over 1965–1995 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get. 6-month momentum computed only inside the top tercile of trailing 6-month share turnover; every other name is held out. Turnover uses today's share count for the whole history because free data has no point-in-time share count, so the tercile split is approximate. Signal is oriented so the direction the paper predicts scores positive, so a negative observed t means the effect ran backwards on this sample.

name: Price
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=2.9 over 1932–1971 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get. Negative log of the unadjusted month-end share price, so cheap stocks are the long side. Uses the split-unadjusted close because the adjusted series distorts the historical price level. Signal is oriented so the direction the paper predicts scores positive, so a negative observed t means the effect ran backwards on this sample.

name: Price delay r square
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=3.4 over 1964–2001 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get. Hou-Moskowitz D1 on a trailing 52 weeks: one minus the ratio of the R-squared from regressing weekly returns on the contemporaneous equal-weighted market return to the R-squared from that regression plus four weekly market lags. Names with a near-zero unrestricted R-squared are held out. Signal is oriented so the direction the paper predicts scores positive, so a negative observed t means the effect ran backwards on this sample.
